judgements.justification: B's Reviewer_VGyX based his 3 partly on the wrong claim that prior work already solved the paper's problem; that work has no learning, and no A reviewer made this error.
A's oral matches ratings 7, 8, 8, 9 (mean 8.0) with no detractor; the chair did not go above the scores.
A's Reviewer_DcW4 gave a generic-praise 9 with no criticism, and B's Reviewer_iVNT gave 9 while admitting confusion about Eq. 2 and Fig. 1; both lifted their committees' ratings.
No flaw was disclosed on one forum only; the camera-ready concessions answer each committee's own reviewers.
A's unanswered rate-lag question was a limitation the reviewer accepted with a promised section, not a substantive flaw the committee ignored.
In A, Reviewer_BSPV raised to an accept (7) after the rebuttal, while no score in B moved.
Only B's VGyX raised the uncited population-response literature (Knight 1972; van Vreeswijk and Sompolinsky 1998) and the sub-biological synaptic time constants; no one in A raised either.
The decisive concerns were raised in B only; the shared realism point did not drive either decision.
B's AC stated an own assessment and accepted with the 9 and 8, adopting VGyX's points as revisions rather than letting him set the outcome.
No reviewer changed score because of other reviews.
The authors answered VGyX's detailed post-rebuttal reply (trial-averaged Köndgen evidence, 6.3 ms AMPA constant) only with thanks, and his 3 stood.
A's Reviewer_DcW4 gave 9 after two hours with generic praise, no questions and no discussion reply, and that 9 counted unchallenged toward the oral.
Neither chair went below its positive majority.
Neither chair decided by a score threshold against its own view.
VGyX's low score rests on the headline fast-computation claim, which is central, not peripheral.
Both committees read the paper as a credit-assignment model; they differed on whether its fast-response claim was new, not on the kind of contribution.
The only reviewer moved by the rebuttal, BSPV, was confident (4) and moved on a limitations section, not on clarifications he could not check.
No committee imposed an extra requirement on this kind of paper.

A's DcW4 gave 9 calling prospective coding unprecedented, though the paper cites Köndgen et al. and co-reviewers cite Brea et al. 2016; B's gRxq praised application to real cortical data that the paper does not use.
VGyX did not concede that the rebuttal answered his concern.
Both committees accepted with revisions; neither refused to credit promised changes.
No reviewer's stated stance diverged from the score.
No extra reviewer was called in.
Clarity verdicts did not split by expertise; both committees found Eq. 2 under-explained.
BSPV stated the reason for his raise; no silent raise.
No chair set aside a silent detractor; VGyX engaged fully.
Both committees had reviewers rating 9 and 8.
No reviewer admitted reading only part of the paper.
VGyX's objection is uncited prior work and time constants, not a rival theoretical school contesting the premise.
A's one-sentence meta-review restates that reviewers agreed on a novel, elegant model and gives no case for an oral over acceptance.
Only B's VGyX knew the population-dynamics literature and checked the fast-response novelty against it; A's reviewers took the novelty at face value, one calling it unprecedented.
A's 'in agreement' is accurate and B's meta-review matches the record.
No one raised breadth of audience.
B's chair adopted the detractor's largely correct points rather than defending acceptance against a misreading.
No new results were posted to one forum only.
B's most expert reviewer rated lowest; no expert high score was outweighed.
VGyX's post-rebuttal text changed no score and the authors could and did reply.
B's 9 and 8 match strongly favourable text; no leniency gap.

added.name: Headline claim judged overstated capped the tier
added.definition: Reviewers or the area chair in one committee judged the paper's headline claim or title overstated relative to what it shows, and held the paper to a lower tier or required the claim to be narrowed, while the other committee took the claim at face value.
added.justification: R07 covers raising an issue the other committee missed, but not the chair's judgement that the paper's headline claim and title promise more than it delivers and that the tier and framing must be cut back accordingly; no other reason names overclaiming as a cause.

reasoning: The gap comes from one confident specialist detractor in B. VGyX showed uncited prior work on faster-than-membrane-time-constant responses and sub-biological synaptic time constants, overreached on the claim that the problem was solved, and B's chair took his points, judging the headline claim overstated and stopping at a poster. A never saw this critique and gave an oral on uniform but thin praise, including a two-hour 9 resting on a wrong novelty claim, with a one-sentence meta-review. Existing reasons cover the missed issue, the literature gap, the thin and inflated praise, the one-sided rebuttal move and the bare meta-review; the overclaiming judgement needed a new reason.
